sources.title: Giving Old Infrastructure New Life
sources.author: Laura Tolkoff
sources.notes: Seen in search results only. "SPUR envisions a megaregional rail network anchored by two types of hubs"; "At the center of the strategy is frequent and reliable service that is available all day." Major multimodal hubs suggested for downtown San Jose, San Francisco, Oakland, Stockton and Sacramento; trains every 15 minutes or better in SF, San Jose and Oakland and every 30 minutes or better in Sacramento, Stockton, Modesto and Merced; a pulse timetable (paraphrase). No line list or map seen.

sources.title: A Vision for Megaregional Rail (event)
sources.notes: Seen in search results only. SPUR and partners propose a rail network for the Northern California megaregion, built on the existing system with targeted investments; anywhere in the Bay Area within an hour and anywhere in the megaregion within 90 minutes (paraphrase).

sources.title: A Mid-Life Crisis for Regional Rail
sources.notes: "Adopted by the SPUR Board of Directors October 17, 2008". Seen in search results only. "The new tube should be designed as a four-track bore to accommodate both BART and standard-gauge rail, such as Caltrain or high speed service." "The San Francisco connection to the tube should be designed with track connections to the Caltrain/High Speed level of the Transbay Transit Center's rail level." The fourth BART track in downtown Oakland: "This is a precursor project to an eventual second Bay Tube." Also an M line link of about a mile from SF State's Holloway stop to Daly City BART, and tunnels through the Altamont Pass and Niles Canyon by 2030 (paraphrase).

sources.title: Muni's Vision for Rapid Transit
sources.notes: Seen in search results only. The article "applies those principles and tools to the corridors, and suggests a list of projects that could become a rapid transit network for San Francisco" (the principles are Muni's). 19th Avenue "is appropriate for surface LRT"; Geary as surface LRT from the ocean to Laguna, then a subway to the Financial District or Transbay Terminal, $1.7 billion; the Central Subway north via Lombard or Chestnut to a Presidio terminal (paraphrase).

sources.title: A New Civic Vision (SPUR Regional Strategy)
sources.notes: Undated. Seen in search results only. sources.title: Designing the Bay Area's Second Transbay Rail Crossing
sources.notes: Landing page: https://www.spur.org/publications/policy-brief/2016-02-10/designing-bay-areas-second-transbay-rail-crossing. Seen in search results only.
